sentenceSets.sentence: After the third increase in two years, the rent on their one-bedroom apartment swallowed nearly half of what the couple earned.

answerChoices.reasoning: A mortgage is what owners pay a bank, but the sentence describes a sum charged on an apartment that keeps being raised by someone else, which is not how a fixed loan payment behaves.
A lease is the agreement itself, so it cannot be the thing that swallows half their earnings; the sentence names an amount of money, not a document.
A fee is a one-time or occasional charge for a service, which does not match a recurring housing cost that consumes half of a couple's income.
Dues are paid by members to an organization they belong to, and nothing in the sentence puts the couple in a club or union.
A deposit is paid once at move-in and returned later, so it could not be raised three times or absorb an ongoing share of their pay.
A surcharge is an extra amount added on top of a base price, whereas the sentence treats this sum as the whole housing cost.
A levy is imposed by a government body, but the sentence locates the charge on their apartment rather than on their income or property taxes.
An installment is one slice of a debt being paid down toward an end point, while the sentence describes a cost that only keeps climbing.
A wage is money the couple receives, and the sentence already contrasts this sum with what they earn.
A dividend is income paid to shareholders, the opposite of an expense that consumes half their pay.
A refund returns money to them and could not swallow any portion of their earnings.

sentenceSets.sentence: The landlord agreed to waive a month's rent while the building's heating system was torn out and replaced.

answerChoices.reasoning: Payment is generic and could name any sum owed to anyone, but the sentence specifies a landlord forgiving a monthly housing charge to tenants enduring construction.
A rate is a price per unit rather than an amount actually due, and one waives money owed, not the pricing formula behind it.
A charge points to a specific billed item, yet the concession here covers an entire month of occupancy rather than one line on a bill.
Board is payment for meals provided with lodging, and the disruption described is to heating, not to any food service.
Insurance is bought from an insurer, not waived by a landlord, and a broken furnace would not suspend a policy.
Maintenance is precisely what the landlord is performing in the sentence, so it is the service being rendered rather than the money being forgiven.
Utilities are metered services billed by suppliers, and waiving them for one month would not be the landlord's to grant in the way the sentence implies.
Interest accrues on borrowed money, and no loan between tenant and landlord appears anywhere in the sentence.
Profit is what the landlord keeps, not a monthly amount he can excuse a tenant from paying.
A salary is paid to an employee, and the sentence describes a building's occupants, not its staff.
A bonus is extra money given out, so waiving one would be a penalty rather than the relief the sentence describes.

sentenceSets.sentence: Because the storefront sat empty through an entire year, the owner finally dropped the rent low enough to tempt a tenant inside.

answerChoices.reasoning: Dropping the price suggests selling the storefront outright, but the sentence's goal is to attract a tenant, someone who occupies rather than buys.
A quote is a figure offered to one prospective customer, whereas the sentence describes a standing amount lowered until anyone would take the space.
A commission is what an agent earns on a deal, and cutting it would motivate the broker rather than the tenant the owner is trying to lure in.
Overhead is the owner's own cost of running the property, which he could reduce without changing anything a prospective tenant sees.
Taxes are set by the municipality, not dropped at an owner's discretion to fill a vacancy.
A valuation is an estimate of worth for accounting or sale purposes and has no direct effect on what a tenant would pay each month.
An appraisal is a professional judgment of value that the owner cannot simply lower himself to attract occupants.
Cutting upkeep would make the empty storefront less appealing, working against the aim of tempting someone inside.
Tuition is charged to students by a school and has no place in a transaction about commercial floor space.
A gratuity is a voluntary tip for service and is not something an owner sets for a vacant shop.
A stipend is money paid out to support someone, the reverse of a sum collected from whoever occupies the storefront.
